comments.note: README.md (Compliance Model): The Authority Hierarchy table correctly positions the Orchestrator as a peer implementation alongside mcp-server/src/, making the language-agnostic scope explicit. The 6 rules are non-redundant and each targets a distinct enforcement concern. Rule 5 ('Implementation notes within the spec are illustrative, not authoritative') is a valuable safeguard against future drift as the TypeScript internals evolve.

constraints.md (Constraint 0): Bidirectional traceability pattern is well-executed. Spec footnotes on constraints 12, 13, 19, 22 (§6.2, §6.5/§21.10, §8, §9/§12 respectively) create navigable cross-references. Constraint 0's scope carve-out ('workflow logic only') is critical — it correctly prevents the spec-first rule from being misapplied to infrastructure concerns (atomic I/O, locking, STDIO) governed by the remaining constraints.

Undeclared artifacts: constraints.md and operations.md were modified but not listed in the implementation pipeline's artifacts array. The changes are thematically correct and cause no harm, but unlisted artifacts reduce ledger traceability — a future audit of what changed in this WP would find an incomplete picture. Future implementation pipelines should declare all modified files regardless of whether they are in-scope or ancillary improvements.

operations.md comment fix: Changing 'Source of truth: CLAIMABLE_ROLES export in ...' to 'Derivation rule defined here (§10.1). Implementation: CLAIMABLE_ROLES export in ...' is a precise correction. The original comment implicitly named the TypeScript module as the authority, directly contradicting the spec-first model this WP establishes. The new wording correctly distinguishes where the rule is defined (the spec) from where it is implemented (the TypeScript export).
